notes: Builds two groups of six character-menu tile masks by filling each 64-byte tile and applying paired XOR masks across seven columns.

2026-08-27: Root cause of the prior draft's 73-differing-halfword score was a mismodeled call. `Func_0800730c` is not a real function: 0x0800730c is the sl (r10) slot of the fourteen-entry `_call_via_rN` trampoline bundle at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (`bx rN; mov r8,r8`, 4 bytes/slot, r0..sp). Unlike the r0-r3 slots (where a fictional trailing argument lands in the right register purely because it's within the 4-register AAPCS/APCS argument window -- see games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/battle/battle_owner_4.c's byte-exact `Func_080072f0(dest,size,value,0x03000168)` precedent for the r3 slot), r10/sl is never an argument-passing register, so no N-argument direct call can ever place a value there; arm_function_arg in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c confirms arguments stop at r3. Rewrote the call as a genuine indirect call through a function-pointer local, `((FillWordsFn)0x03000168)(tile, 64, 0x44444444)` (FillWordsFn = void(*)(void*,s32,u32)), matching the already-adopted indirect-call idiom in games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c. This alone let the compiler naturally allocate both sl (the fill-routine pointer, loop-invariant) and r8 (the Data_080af23c base, loop-invariant) exactly as the reference does, dropping differing_halfwords from 73 to 6 (wrong_instructions 22->0) with zero remaining structural/semantic mismatches -- the rest of the function's control flow, mask-index clamp, and loop nesting were already correct in the prior draft.

2026-08-27 (same pass): the residual 6 differing halfwords were pure instruction-scheduling reordering (class=ordering, wrong_instructions=0): the reference finishes `tile[column] ^= Data_080af23c[mask_index].left;` completely (load, xor, store) before starting any part of the second statement's address advance, while the naive two-statement candidate let the compiler hoist the independent `adds r1,#4`/`mov r3,r8` (address setup for `.right`) forward into the middle of the first statement's dependency chain. Tried and rejected (each scored worse or unchanged, all still available in this dossier via the permuter's report.json runs during this session): swapping statement order; explicit non-compound `a = a ^ b` forms; wrapping just one statement in an empty block (no effect -- proves the fix isn't about lexical block boundaries per se); an unused/dead local declared in the block (no effect -- proves it isn't about the block merely containing a declaration); a named local `struct TileMaskPair *mask`/`masks[]` pointer alias for the whole Data_080af23c[mask_index] pair (regressed hard, 39-47 diff, evidently disturbs the loop-invariant hoisting of the array base entirely); flat `(const u8*)Data_080af23c + mask_index*8` byte-offset addressing (regressed to candidate=156, 75 diff). The fix that worked: materializing only the `.left` value into a named local (`u32 left = Data_080af23c[mask_index].left;`) as its own full statement, immediately before `tile[column] ^= left;`, inside a fresh nested block. This is a real, minimal, plausible source shape (a natural place to name the first mask half) and it fixed the scheduling exactly: differing_halfwords 6->4.

2026-08-27 (same pass, residual documented, not fully closed): the remaining 4 differing halfwords (wrong_instructions=8, class=allocation, matched_prefix=37 of 74) are a register-role swap confined to the single `eors`/`str` pair for the `.left` xor: reference computes `mov r3,r8; ldr r3,[r3,r1]` (mask value REUSES r3, the now-dead address-base register) then `ldr r2,[r0,#0]` (tile value gets a fresh r2), `eors r2,r3`, `str r2,[r0,#0]`; the candidate instead gives the mask value a fresh r2 and lets the tile value reuse r3, i.e. `eors r3,r2; str r3,[r0,#0]` -- functionally identical, byte-different. Root cause, confirmed by direct A/B compiles: naming `left` as a real local (required to fix the scheduling above) makes GCC give it its OWN fresh pseudo/register rather than letting it merge into the about-to-be-dead address-base register the way an anonymous temporary can; reversing which value is named first (naming a `tile[column]` temp `t0` ahead of `left`) restores the correct r2/r3 roles for this pair but reintroduces the exact scheduling bug fixed above (verified: byte-identical output to the pre-fix 6-diff candidate). Every combination tried this pass of naming order, naming only one side, pointer-vs-value naming, `s32`-cast naming, comma-expression forced evaluation order, and prefetching `.right` first instead of `.left` either reproduced one of these two mutually exclusive outcomes exactly or regressed further (see the permuter runs from this pass, not retained on disk but reproducible via the PERM_GENERAL alternatives documented here). This looks like a genuine tension in this compiler's local-alloc between named-variable register independence and anonymous-temporary register reuse for this exact code shape, not yet resolved -- kept the scheduling-correct, semantically-clean variant (4 diff) rather than the roles-correct-but-misordered variant (6 diff) since it is closer to exact and the residual is a stable, well-characterized 2-instruction-pair swap, not a semantic error. Did not force register assignment via `register`-qualified locals, named-register variables, or inline asm, per project rules. Worth a future pass with a different local-alloc lever now that the swap is precisely characterized.

Adoption gate not met: differing_halfwords=4, not 0. Candidate is otherwise structurally and semantically complete -- no remaining algorithm, control-flow, or type mismatches, only the documented register-role swap above.
